https://hungarytoday.hu/no-pm-magyar-lef.text: “NO!” PM Magyar Left Red-faced after Rejection from His Presidential Choice Hungary’s autocratic leader faces public humiliation as his choice as an interim president replacing the undemocratically removed Tamás Sulyok has rejected his offer. Chess grandmaster Judit Polgár has made it clear that she does not want to become the president of a deeply divided nation. Only weeks after the cringe-worthy scenes at the NATO Summit in Ankara on July 7, when he unsuccessfully tried but failed to shake hands with the U.S. President, Péter Magyar has run into another humiliation of his own device. On Monday, a day after the controversial forced removal of President Tamás Sulyok that commenters dubbed “political violence,” he approached famous Hungarian chess grandmaster Judit Polgár to become interim president until the new amendment of the constitution takes place. Hours passed by and the nation was holding its breath, as it slowly became clear that Polgár may not want to fill the role so comprehensively discredited by the politically motivated campaign against the previous president. Finally, late in the afternoon, the news broke that she will not accept Magyar’s offer. In her explanation on social media, she wrote: “I consider it the greatest honor of my life to have been nominated by the initiators for the office of President of the Republic, and I am deeply grateful for this. I greatly appreciate the Prime Minister’s gesture in nominating an independent candidate who stands above party politics for the office of President of the Republic, despite his party’s significant parliamentary influence.” At the same time, I do not feel I have the strength to take on the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation, and so I am unable to accept the nomination.” “I will do everything in my power to support a new, independent, and respected President of the Republic in achieving these goals,” concluded Polgár. A spectacular celebration – and a very special game with @magyarpeterMP ! Happy Birthday, America! 🇺🇸 #ChessConnectsUs @usembbudapest @Rubiks_Official pic.twitter.com/oEWRb3YYmK — Judit Polgar (@GMJuditPolgar) July 3, 2026 Most commenters have hailed Polgár’s deicision as wise and one that will safeguard her reputation and lifetime achievements. Although she is widely considered as truly apolitical, from the photos of her earlier meeting with Magyar, as well as her enthusiasm for George Soros, it is clear that the chess prodigy is not naturally associated with the national-conservative side. Although Polgár was awarded a HUF 700 million grant (EUR 2 million) for her chess academy project from the Orbán government in 2021, she has largely stayed out of politics and never commented on current affairs. Whether it was the grave responsibility for uniting a divided nation, her lack of experience in constitutional matters, her Israeli-Hungarian double citizenship , or the reputational damage anyone will almost inevitably suffer accepting this tainted post that made her refuse the offer, is anyone’s guess. It’s impressive how George Soros plays chess and has pretty good opening repertoire! Great chess evening 🙂 pic.twitter.com/mZGEr9ksPj — Judit Polgar (@GMJuditPolgar) April 22, 2014 Magyar will clearly need to reach very low now to find a person willing to fill this most controversial position in Hungarian politics. After the scandalous removal of Tamás Sulyok and the very public humiliation suffered at the hand of the queen of the chess board, he will probably be forced to source the new interim president from the ranks of his staunchest loyalists. Whoever will succeed him, Sulyok’s last words will inevitably echo in his successor’s mind. In his parting video message to the nation, the outgoing head of state said that “the legitimacy of the president of the Republic, which had remained unchanged since the transition to democracy, has ceased to exist. Hungary’s next head of state will, in fact, replace a president who was removed through a process that violated constitutional values.” The office of the president of the Republic will become subservient to the executive branch and politics; its role under public law will fade, and its fundamental function will cease to exist. Furthermore, it will no longer serve as any kind of check or balance.” Thirty-six years after gaining freedom from under the Soviet yoke, Hungary slides back into dictatorship.
